body.iCan: I can read a short story or poem.
successCriteria: I can read and understand a short literary text or artwork in Spanish

body.hook: Pablo Neruda, a Chilean poet, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971. He wrote love poems and also odes to ordinary things: a tomato, socks, an onion. Spanish-language literature and art often find the extraordinary in the everyday.

vocabulary.definition: The image (in a poem or painting).

study.title: Arte y palabras
study.question: How do I interpret Spanish-language literature and art?
study.passage:
Option 1, Poetry: Pablo Neruda (Chile, 1904–1973) wrote "Odas elementales" (1954), odes to simple things. Read a short excerpt chosen by the teacher from "Oda al tomate" or "Oda a los calcetines." Identify images (comparisons with sun, fire, jewels) and the theme: ordinary things are beautiful and worth celebrating.
Option 2, Art: Frida Kahlo (Mexico, 1907–1954) painted many self-portraits that show her identity, Mexican culture and physical pain after a bus accident. Look at "Las dos Fridas" (1939): two Fridas sit side by side, one in a European dress and one in a Tehuana dress, their hearts connected.
Analysis vocabulary: El tema es... / El autor usa la imagen de... para mostrar... / Los colores representan... / Creo que el mensaje es... / Me hace sentir...
Modelo de análisis: En "Las dos Fridas", la pintora muestra dos partes de su identidad: la europea y la mexicana. Las dos mujeres se toman de la mano, y sus corazones están conectados. Creo que el mensaje es que su identidad tiene dos raíces. El cielo oscuro me hace sentir tristeza.
Task: Choose a poem or painting. Answer comprehension questions, then write an interpretation using the analysis phrases.
study.source: Analysis written for this lesson; works are by Pablo Neruda (1954) and Frida Kahlo (1939); teachers provide approved excerpts and images.
steps: Read a poem excerpt or view a painting
discussion: ¿Por qué Neruda escribe sobre cosas simples?
study.product: Write a 150-word interpretation in Spanish of a poem or painting: describe it, explain two images or symbols, state the theme and give your personal response.

examples.title: Theme
examples.problem: What is the theme of Neruda's odes?
examples.answer: Ordinary things are beautiful and worth celebrating

examples.title: Image
examples.problem: In "Las dos Fridas," what do the connected hearts show?
examples.answer: The two sides of her identity are linked

examples.title: Phrase
examples.problem: Say "The author uses the image of the sun to show joy."
examples.answer: El autor usa la imagen del sol para mostrar alegría.

examples.title: Response
examples.problem: Say "The painting makes me feel sad."
examples.answer: El cuadro me hace sentir triste (tristeza).

practice.q: What do the two dresses in "Las dos Fridas" represent?
Translate: I think the message is...
Why might Neruda write odes to socks and tomatoes?
practice.a: To show beauty in everyday life.

practice.q: How does Kahlo use self-portraits to explore identity?
practice.a: By showing different parts of herself, her culture and her pain.

practice.q: Write a sentence interpreting a colour in a painting.
Why is personal response part of interpretation?
practice.a: Art and poetry create meaning through the reader's or viewer's experience too.

misconceptions: Thinking there is only one correct interpretation
exitTicket: Name one image in the work and its meaning.
Write one sentence with "me hace sentir."
